title: 9.2 Small Group · Group 1
contentObjective: With my small group, I can use a table and a graph to determine and analyze the relationship between two variable quantities — one step at a time, with support.
languageObjective: I can talk through each step out loud using a sentence frame and the lesson's key words.

vocabulary.definition: A picture on a coordinate plane that shows how two quantities are related.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un dibujo en un plano de coordenadas que muestra cómo se relacionan dos cantidades.
vocabulary.example: The football ticket graph shows cost rising as tickets increase.
vocabulary.visual: Points (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135) climbing left to right — cost by tickets.
vocabulary.cloze: A picture on the coordinate plane showing how two quantities relate is a ___.

examples.text: Plotted points where each one is a (tickets, cost) pair
examples.why: Every point carries both quantities at once.
A picture with no quantities on it shows no relationship.

vocabulary.definition: A list of matched pairs of values that shows a relationship using numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una lista de pares de valores que muestra una relación usando números.
vocabulary.example: The ticket table pairs 3 tickets with $135.
vocabulary.visual: months 1, 2, 4 beside cost 24.95, 49.90, 99.80 — one row per pair.
vocabulary.cloze: A list of matched pairs that shows a relationship in numbers is a ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Hours in one column, kilometers in the other
examples.why: Each row pairs the two quantities at the same moment.

examples.text: A column of costs with nothing to pair them to
examples.why: One quantity alone shows no relationship.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers written as (x, y) that name one point on a graph. The independent variable comes first.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números escritos como (x, y) que nombran un punto en la gráfica. La variable independiente va primero.
vocabulary.visual: (3, 135): 3 tickets cost $135 — the independent quantity comes first.
vocabulary.cloze: Two numbers written (x, y) that name one point are an ___ ___.

examples.why: Reversed, it plots a different point.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two number lines that frame a graph. Each axis is labeled with a quantity from the problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una de las dos rectas numéricas que enmarcan una gráfica. Cada eje se rotula con una cantidad del problema.
vocabulary.example: One axis shows the number of tickets; the other shows the total cost.
vocabulary.visual: Horizontal axis: months. Vertical axis: total cost.
vocabulary.cloze: Each number line framing a graph, labeled with a quantity, is an ___.

examples.text: The horizontal line labeled “number of tickets”
examples.why: It is one of the two lines, and it names a quantity.

examples.text: The line connecting the plotted points
examples.why: That shows the trend; it does not frame the graph.

vocabulary.definition: The numbers in an ordered pair that tell how far to move along each axis to reach a point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los números de un par ordenado que indican cuánto avanzar por cada eje para llegar a un punto.
vocabulary.example: The coordinates of the tram point (5, 6000) are 5 minutes and 6,000 feet.
vocabulary.visual: In (4, 105), 4 says how far across and 105 how far up.
vocabulary.cloze: The numbers in an ordered pair that tell how far to move are its ___.

examples.why: They locate the point on each axis.
A label names an axis; it is not a number.

turnAndTalk.question: Football tickets cost $45 each: 1 ticket is $45, 2 tickets are $90, 3 tickets are $135. When you write the ordered pair for 3 tickets, which number goes first — 3 or 135 — and why?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The number of tickets is the independent variable, and the independent variable always comes first in an ordered pair, so the point is (3, 135), not (135, 3).

stems.en: The ordered pair is (___, ___) because ___ comes first.
stems.es: El par ordenado es (___, ___) porque ___ va primero.

stems.en: If I wrote (135, 3) instead, that would mean ___.
stems.es: Si escribiera (135, 3) en cambio, eso significaría ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute. Justify why the point for 5 minutes is (5, 6000) and not (6000, 5), using the same rule you used for the tickets.
extendStems: Minutes is independent because ___, so it goes ___ in the pair.
(6000, 5) would be wrong because it would mean ___.

turnAndTalk.question: You sorted cards like '(4, 190) is a point on the graph' into matches and non-matches for cost = 45 × tickets. How did you check each one?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A point (tickets, cost) matches the relationship only if cost equals 45 times the number of tickets.

stems.en: I checked (___, ___) by multiplying ___ × 45 and comparing it to ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Card '(1, 55) is a point on the graph' was also NOT a match. What single mistake would produce 55 instead of the correct value — and how is that different from the mistake in (4, 190)?
extendStems: 55 could come from ___ instead of multiplying, while 190 looks like a different kind of error: ___.
Both are wrong, but for different reasons: ___ versus ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Nakai's account starts with $750 and earns the same $26.25 every year. Why does the interest graph rise in a straight line instead of curving upward more steeply each year?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Simple interest is calculated only on the original $750 principal, so the SAME amount, $26.25, is added every year — a constant increase makes a straight line, not a curve.

stems.en: The graph is straight because every year adds exactly $___.
stems.es: La gráfica es recta porque cada año se suman exactamente $___.

stems.en: If the interest grew faster each year, that would mean ___ instead of simple interest.
stems.es: Si el interés creciera más rápido cada año, eso significaría ___ en lugar de interés simple.

turnAndTalk.extend: A point on Nakai's graph is (4, x). Find x, and explain how you know your answer is NOT the account's total balance after 4 years.
extendStems: x = ___ because 4 years of $26.25 each is 4 × ___.
That is not the total balance because the balance would also include the ___ of $750.

turnAndTalk.question: Look back at a problem where you found coordinates for a point. What was your process from the rate to the final ordered pair?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Every ordered pair on a rate graph comes from multiplying the rate by the independent variable's value, then writing (independent, dependent).

stems.en: I started with the rate, $___ per ___, then multiplied by ___ to get the total.
stems.es: Empecé con la tasa, $___ por ___, luego multipliqué por ___ para obtener el total.

stems.en: I know my ordered pair is correct because ___.
stems.es: Sé que mi par ordenado es correcto porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate wrote the point for 4 tickets as (4, 49) instead of (4, 180). What operation mistake would produce 49, and how would you help them catch it?
extendStems: 49 looks like they ___ instead of multiplying 4 × 45.
I'd tell them to check by ___ before trusting the answer.

launch.narrative: This is your support small group for Lesson 9.2. We're going to slow this down and build it together, one step at a time. You can ask a question any time — that's what this group is for.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — Two pictures of the same relationship
conceptIntro.intro: A table shows a relationship with numbers. A graph shows the same relationship with points. Reading either one tells you how the dependent variable responds to the independent variable. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Each row of the table becomes one ordered pair — (independent variable, dependent variable) — plotted as one point on the graph.

iDo.title: Watch me build the ticket graph
lines: Each ticket costs $45, so the total cost is 45 times the number of tickets: 1 ticket is $45, 2 tickets are $90, 3 tickets are $135.
The number of tickets is the independent variable, so it goes first in each ordered pair: (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135).
I label one axis 'Number of tickets' and the other 'Total cost ($)', then plot each pair as a point.
The points rise to the right: as the number of tickets increases, the total cost increases.
linesEs: Cada boleto cuesta $45, así que el costo total es 45 por el número de boletos: 1 boleto son $45, 2 boletos son $90, 3 boletos son $135.
El número de boletos es la variable independiente, así que va primero en cada par ordenado: (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135).
Rotulo un eje como «Número de boletos» y el otro como «Costo total ($)», y luego marco cada par como un punto.
Los puntos suben hacia la derecha: conforme aumenta el número de boletos, aumenta el costo total.
iDo.titleEs: Mírame armar la gráfica de los boletos

weDo.title: Let's graph the Sandia Peak tram together
lines: The tram travels 1,200 feet every minute. Which quantity is independent — time or distance?
Time is independent, so our pairs look like (minutes, feet): (1, 1200), (2, 2400), (5, 6000).
The ascent takes 15 minutes, so the last point is (15, 18000) — because 15 times 1,200 is 18,000 feet.
Each point means: after THIS many minutes, the tram has traveled THIS many feet.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."
linesEs: El teleférico recorre 1,200 pies cada minuto. ¿Qué cantidad es independiente — el tiempo o la distancia?
El tiempo es independiente, así que nuestros pares se ven como (minutos, pies): (1, 1200), (2, 2400), (5, 6000).
El ascenso toma 15 minutos, así que el último punto es (15, 18000) — porque 15 por 1,200 son 18,000 pies.
Cada punto significa: después de estos minutos, el teleférico ha recorrido estos pies.
Marco de oración — dilo conmigo: «Mi primer paso es ___ , porque el problema pide ___ .»
weDo.titleEs: Grafiquemos juntos el teleférico de Sandia Peak

conceptIntro.headingEs: Construyámoslo juntos — Dos imágenes de la misma relación
conceptIntro.introEs: Una tabla muestra una relación con números. Una gráfica muestra la misma relación con puntos. Leer cualquiera de las dos te dice cómo responde la variable dependiente a la independiente. Veremos un ejemplo resuelto, haremos uno juntos y luego harás algunos con pistas disponibles cuando las necesites.

connect.scenario: Nakai opened a savings account with an initial deposit, or principal, of $750. The account earns 3.5% simple interest each year — interest is the amount earned for the use of the principal. A graph shows the interest Nakai has earned over a period of years, with points rising steadily.
connect.promptQuestion: What observations can you make about the data using the graph?
connect.prompt: ___ is the independent variable, while ___ is the dependent variable. As the years go by, the interest earned ___, because each year adds $___ to the total.

check.stem: On Nakai's graph, which variable is plotted on the independent axis (x-axis)?
check.explanation: Years is the independent variable because interest earned changes as a result of how many years have passed, not the other way around. Interest earned is dependent; the principal ($750) is a fixed starting value, not a changing quantity being graphed; account balance combines principal and interest, which isn't what this graph plots.
check.stemEs: En la gráfica de Nakai, ¿qué variable se marca en el eje independiente (el eje x)?
check.explanationEs: Los años son la variable independiente porque el interés ganado cambia como resultado de cuántos años han pasado, no al revés. El interés ganado es dependiente; el capital ($750) es un valor inicial fijo, no una cantidad que cambia y se grafica; el saldo de la cuenta combina capital e interés, que no es lo que grafica esta gráfica.

check.stem: Why does the graph rise by the same amount every year instead of curving upward more steeply over time?
choices: Nakai earns compound interest, which grows faster each year
The interest rate increases by 3.5% every year
Nakai deposits an extra $26.25 into the account every year
Nakai earns simple interest — the same $26.25 each year, calculated only on the original $750 principal
check.explanation: Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal each year, so the account gains a constant $26.25 annually, producing a straight (linear) rise. Compound interest would make the graph curve upward faster, a rising rate would change the yearly amount, and extra deposits would not be interest at all.
check.stemEs: ¿Por qué sube la gráfica la misma cantidad cada año en vez de curvarse hacia arriba más pronunciadamente con el tiempo?
check.explanationEs: El interés simple se calcula solo sobre el capital original cada año, así que la cuenta gana $26.25 constantes al año, produciendo una subida recta (lineal). El interés compuesto haría que la gráfica se curvara hacia arriba más rápido, una tasa creciente cambiaría la cantidad anual, y los depósitos extra no serían interés.
choicesEs: Nakai gana interés compuesto, que crece más rápido cada año
La tasa de interés aumenta 3.5% cada año
Nakai deposita $26.25 extra en la cuenta cada año
Nakai gana interés simple — los mismos $26.25 cada año, calculados solo sobre el capital original de $750

check.stem: A point on the graph is located at (4, x). Based on the interest rate, what value of x makes this point correct?
check.explanation: After 4 years Nakai has earned 4 × $26.25 = $105 in interest. $78.75 is only 3 years' worth of interest, $855 confuses interest earned with the total account balance (principal plus interest), and $131.25 is 5 years' worth.
check.stemEs: Un punto de la gráfica está en (4, x). Según la tasa de interés, ¿qué valor de x hace correcto este punto?
check.explanationEs: Después de 4 años Nakai ha ganado 4 × $26.25 = $105 de interés. $78.75 es solo el interés de 3 años, $855 confunde el interés ganado con el saldo total de la cuenta (capital más interés), y $131.25 es el de 5 años.

connect.modelAnswer: The number of years is the independent variable and the interest earned is the dependent variable. The graph rises steadily because Nakai earns the same amount every year — 3.5% of $750 is $26.25. A point like (2, 52.50) means that after 2 years Nakai has earned $52.50 in interest, since 2 × 26.25 = 52.50.
connect.promptEs: ___ es la variable independiente, mientras que ___ es la variable dependiente. Conforme pasan los años, el interés ganado ___, porque cada año le suma $___ al total.
connect.scenarioEs: Nakai abrió una cuenta de ahorros con un depósito inicial, o capital, de $750. La cuenta gana 3.5% de interés simple cada año — el interés es la cantidad ganada por el uso del capital. Una gráfica muestra el interés que Nakai ha ganado a lo largo de varios años, con puntos que suben de manera constante.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Qué observaciones puedes hacer sobre los datos usando la gráfica?
connect.modelAnswerEs: El número de años es la variable independiente y el interés ganado es la variable dependiente. La gráfica sube de manera constante porque Nakai gana la misma cantidad cada año — el 3.5% de $750 son $26.25. Un punto como (2, 52.50) significa que después de 2 años Nakai ha ganado $52.50 de interés, ya que 2 × 26.25 = 52.50.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: On the football ticket graph, what does the point (3, 135) represent?
exitTicket.explanation: The independent variable comes first in an ordered pair. Here that is the number of tickets, so 3 is the tickets. Then find the cost: 3 × $45 = $135. The point pairs 3 tickets with a total cost of $135.
hints: Which quantity comes first in an ordered pair — the independent or dependent variable?
The number of tickets is the independent variable here.
Check the arithmetic: what is 3 × 45?
exitTicket.stemEs: Revisión rápida — tú puedes: En la gráfica de boletos de fútbol americano, ¿qué representa el punto (3, 135)?
exitTicket.explanationEs: La variable independiente va primero en un par ordenado. Aquí esa es el número de boletos, así que el 3 son los boletos. Luego halla el costo: 3 × $45 = $135. El punto empareja 3 boletos con un costo total de $135.
hintsEs: ¿Qué cantidad va primero en un par ordenado — la variable independiente o la dependiente?
El número de boletos es la variable independiente aquí.
Revisa la aritmética: ¿cuánto es 3 × 45?

approaching.stem: Football tickets cost $45 each. What is the total cost of 3 tickets?
approaching.explanation: The total cost is 45 times the number of tickets, and 3 × 45 = 135.
choiceFeedback: $45 is the cost of just 1 ticket.
That adds 45 + 3 instead of multiplying 45 × 3.
$90 is the cost of 2 tickets, not 3.
hints: What is the cost of ONE ticket?
Each of the 3 tickets adds another $45.
Multiply the price of one ticket by the number of tickets.
approaching.stemEs: Los boletos de fútbol americano cuestan $45 cada uno. ¿Cuál es el costo total de 3 boletos?
approaching.explanationEs: El costo total es 45 por el número de boletos, y 3 × 45 = 135.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el costo de UN boleto?
Cada uno de los 3 boletos suma otros $45.
Multiplica el precio de un boleto por el número de boletos.

approaching.stem: Which ordered pair belongs on the ticket graph for 2 tickets?
approaching.explanation: The number of tickets goes first, and 2 tickets cost 2 × 45 = 90 dollars, so the point is (2, 90).
choiceFeedback: $45 is the cost of 1 ticket, not 2.
That adds 45 + 2 instead of multiplying 45 × 2.
You reversed the coordinates — the independent variable (tickets) goes first.
hints: Which quantity goes first in the ordered pair?
Tickets is the independent variable, so it comes first.
The second number is 2 × 45.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál par ordenado corresponde a 2 boletos en la gráfica de boletos?
approaching.explanationEs: El número de boletos va primero, y 2 boletos cuestan 2 × 45 = 90 dólares, así que el punto es (2, 90).
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad va primero en el par ordenado?
Los boletos son la variable independiente, así que van primero.
El segundo número es 2 × 45.

approaching.stem: On the ticket graph, what should the two axes be labeled?
choices: Number of tickets and price of one ticket
Number of tickets and total cost
Number of games and number of tickets
approaching.explanation: Each axis is labeled with one quantity from the problem — one axis shows the number of tickets and the other shows the total cost.
choiceFeedback: The price of one ticket is fixed at $45 — it is not a changing quantity, so it does not get an axis.
$45 is a fixed rate, not a variable quantity that gets its own axis.
The number of games is not one of the two quantities in this problem.
hints: Which TWO quantities change in this situation?
One is the choice; the other responds to it.
You choose the tickets, and the total cost responds.
approaching.stemEs: En la gráfica de boletos, ¿cómo se deben rotular los dos ejes?
approaching.explanationEs: Cada eje se rotula con una cantidad del problema — un eje muestra el número de boletos y el otro muestra el costo total.
hintsEs: ¿Cuáles DOS cantidades cambian en esta situación?
Uno es lo que se escoge; el otro responde a eso.
Tú escoges los boletos, y el costo total responde.
choicesEs: Número de boletos y precio de un boleto
Número de boletos y costo total
Número de juegos y número de boletos

approaching.stem: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute. How far has it traveled after 3 minutes?
approaching.explanation: The tram covers 1,200 feet every minute, so after 3 minutes it has gone 3 × 1,200 = 3,600 feet.
choiceFeedback: 1,200 feet is the distance after only 1 minute.
That adds 1,200 + 3 instead of multiplying 1,200 × 3.
2,400 feet is the distance after 2 minutes, not 3.
hints: How far does the tram go in ONE minute?
Each minute adds another 1,200 feet.
Multiply 1,200 by the number of minutes.
approaching.stemEs: El tranvía de Sandia Peak recorre 1,200 pies por minuto. ¿Qué distancia ha recorrido después de 3 minutos?
approaching.explanationEs: El tranvía recorre 1,200 pies cada minuto, así que después de 3 minutos ha avanzado 3 × 1,200 = 3,600 pies.
hintsEs: ¿Qué distancia recorre el tranvía en UN minuto?
Cada minuto suma otros 1,200 pies.
Multiplica 1,200 por el número de minutos.

approaching.instructions: Football tickets cost $45 each, so the graph follows c = 45t. Sort each ordered pair: is it on the ticket graph or not?
approaching.instructionsEs: Los boletos de fútbol americano cuestan $45 cada uno, así que la gráfica sigue c = 45t. Clasifica cada par ordenado: ¿está en la gráfica o no?
approaching.label: Sort each ordered pair (tickets, cost): on the graph, or not?
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada par ordenado (boletos, costo): ¿está en la gráfica o no?
hints: Test each pair: does the cost equal 45 × the tickets?
3 tickets should cost 3 × 45 = 135 — compare that to what the pair claims.
hintsEs: Prueba cada par: ¿el costo es igual a 45 × los boletos?
3 boletos deberían costar 3 × 45 = 135: compara eso con lo que afirma el par.
approaching.explanation: A point belongs on the graph only when its y-value is exactly 45 times its x-value: 45, 90, and 180 pass. The impostors fail the test: 3 tickets cost 135 (not 120), 2 tickets cost 90 (not 100), and 5 tickets cost 225 (not 200). Checking a point against the rule is how a graph is read, not just drawn.
approaching.explanationEs: Un punto pertenece a la gráfica solo cuando su valor y es exactamente 45 veces su valor x: 45, 90 y 180 pasan. Los impostores fallan: 3 boletos cuestan 135 (no 120), 2 cuestan 90 (no 100) y 5 cuestan 225 (no 200). Verificar un punto contra la regla es la forma de leer una gráfica, no solo de dibujarla.

approaching.label: Tickets cost $45 each. Complete the table that feeds the graph.
approaching.labelEs: Los boletos cuestan $45 cada uno. Completa la tabla que alimenta la gráfica.
hints: The independent variable (tickets) goes in column 1; the dependent (cost) responds in the last column.
Each completed row becomes one point on the graph: (tickets, cost).
hintsEs: La variable independiente (boletos) va en la columna 1; la dependiente (costo) responde en la última columna.
Cada fila completada se convierte en un punto de la gráfica: (boletos, costo).
approaching.explanation: Each row multiplies by the $45 rate: (2, 90), (5, 225), (8, 360). Those three rows ARE three points of the graph — a table and a graph are two views of the same relationship, which is the central idea of this lesson.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada fila multiplica por la tarifa de $45: (2, 90), (5, 225), (8, 360). Esas tres filas son tres puntos de la gráfica: una tabla y una gráfica son dos vistas de la misma relación, la idea central de esta lección.

onLevel.stem: A table shows a train traveling 48 kilometers every hour: 1 hour, 48 km; 5 hours, 240 km. How many kilometers does it travel in 2 hours?
onLevel.explanation: At 48 kilometers per hour, 2 hours gives 2 × 48 = 96 kilometers.
choiceFeedback: 48 km is the distance for 1 hour, not 2.
That adds 48 + 2 instead of multiplying 48 × 2.
144 km is the distance for 3 hours, not 2.
hints: How far in ONE hour?
Each hour adds another 48 km.
Multiply 48 by 2.
onLevel.stemEs: Una tabla muestra un tren que viaja 48 kilómetros cada hora: 1 hora, 48 km; 5 horas, 240 km. ¿Cuántos kilómetros viaja en 2 horas?
onLevel.explanationEs: A 48 kilómetros por hora, 2 horas dan 2 × 48 = 96 kilómetros.
hintsEs: ¿Qué distancia en UNA hora?
Cada hora suma otros 48 km.
Multiplica 48 por 2.

onLevel.stem: As the number of tickets purchased increases, the total cost…
onLevel.explanation: Every extra ticket adds another $45, so the total cost rises as the number of tickets rises.
choiceFeedback: Buying MORE tickets cannot make the total go down — each ticket adds $45.
The table shows different totals ($45, $90, $135), so the cost does not stay the same.
The relationship is clear from the table: more tickets always means a higher total.
hints: Compare the totals for 1, 2, and 3 tickets.
$45, $90, $135 — which direction is that going?
Each new ticket adds to the total.
onLevel.stemEs: Conforme aumenta el número de boletos comprados, el costo total…
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada boleto adicional suma otros $45, así que el costo total sube conforme sube el número de boletos.
hintsEs: Compara los totales de 1, 2 y 3 boletos.
$45, $90, $135 — ¿en qué dirección va eso?
Cada boleto nuevo se suma al total.

onLevel.stem: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute and the ascent takes 15 minutes. How long is the whole ascent in feet?
choiceFeedback: That adds 1,200 + 15 instead of multiplying 1,200 × 15.
12,000 feet is the distance after 10 minutes, not the full 15.
16,800 feet is the distance after 14 minutes — one minute short of the top.
hints: How many minutes does the full ascent take?
Each of those 15 minutes covers 1,200 feet.
Multiply 1,200 by 15.
onLevel.stemEs: El tranvía de Sandia Peak recorre 1,200 pies por minuto y el ascenso toma 15 minutos. ¿Cuánto mide todo el ascenso en pies?
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos minutos toma todo el ascenso?
Cada uno de esos 15 minutos cubre 1,200 pies.
Multiplica 1,200 por 15.

onLevel.stem: On the tram graph with minutes on the horizontal axis and feet on the vertical axis, which ordered pair lies on the graph?
onLevel.explanation: After 5 minutes the tram has traveled 5 × 1,200 = 6,000 feet, so the point is (5, 6000).
choiceFeedback: 1,200 feet is the distance for 1 minute, not 5.
5,000 rounds the rate to 1,000 feet per minute — the tram travels 1,200 feet each minute.
You reversed the coordinates — time (the independent variable) goes first.
hints: Which axis is time on?
The second coordinate is the distance after 5 minutes.
Multiply 5 by 1,200.
onLevel.stemEs: En la gráfica del tranvía con los minutos en el eje horizontal y los pies en el eje vertical, ¿cuál par ordenado está en la gráfica?
onLevel.explanationEs: Después de 5 minutos el tranvía ha recorrido 5 × 1,200 = 6,000 pies, así que el punto es (5, 6000).
hintsEs: ¿En cuál eje va el tiempo?
La segunda coordenada es la distancia después de 5 minutos.
Multiplica 5 por 1,200.

onLevel.stem: A table pairs hours with kilometers: (1, 48), (2, 96), (5, 240). How many kilometers are traveled each hour?
onLevel.explanation: Look for what each row multiplies by. Check the second row: 2 × 48 = 96. Check the third: 5 × 48 = 240. Every row is 48 times the hours, so the rate is 48 kilometers per hour.
choiceFeedback: 24 splits 48 in half, but the table shows 48 km in the very first hour.
96 km is the distance for 2 hours — divide it by 2 to get the rate for 1 hour.
240 km is the distance for 5 hours, not the per-hour rate.
hints: Look at the row for 1 hour.
Check it with another row: does 2 hours give twice as much?
The rate is the distance for exactly one hour.
onLevel.stemEs: Una tabla relaciona horas con kilómetros: (1, 48), (2, 96), (5, 240). ¿Cuántos kilómetros se recorren cada hora?
onLevel.explanationEs: Busca por cuánto se multiplica cada fila. Revisa la segunda: 2 × 48 = 96. Revisa la tercera: 5 × 48 = 240. Cada fila es 48 por las horas, así que la tasa es 48 kilómetros por hora.
hintsEs: Mira la fila de 1 hora.
Compruébalo con otra fila: ¿2 horas dan el doble?
La tasa es la distancia de exactamente una hora.

onLevel.stem: Why is the line on the football ticket graph dashed instead of solid?
choices: Dashed lines always mean the cost is decreasing
The ticket price changes between points
You can only buy whole numbers of tickets, so the points between whole numbers do not make sense
onLevel.explanation: You cannot buy 2.5 tickets. So only the whole-number points represent real purchases. The dashes still show the trend between them. They just do not claim the in-between points are possible.
choiceFeedback: The graph is complete — the dashes are a deliberate choice about what the in-between values mean.
Dashes say nothing about direction; this cost is increasing.
The price stays $45 per ticket everywhere on the graph.
hints: Could you buy half a ticket?
Which points on the line represent real purchases?
Only whole numbers of tickets make sense here.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Por qué la línea de la gráfica de boletos de fútbol americano es punteada en vez de continua?
onLevel.explanationEs: No puedes comprar 2.5 boletos. Así que solo los puntos con números enteros representan compras reales. Las líneas punteadas muestran la tendencia entre ellos. Simplemente no afirman que los puntos intermedios sean posibles.
hintsEs: ¿Podrías comprar medio boleto?
¿Cuáles puntos de la línea representan compras reales?
Aquí solo tienen sentido los números enteros de boletos.
choicesEs: Las líneas punteadas siempre significan que el costo está bajando
El precio del boleto cambia entre un punto y otro
Solo se pueden comprar números enteros de boletos, así que los puntos entre números enteros no tienen sentido

onLevel.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: On the ticket graph, what should the two axes be labeled?
workedExample.workEs: En la gráfica de boletos, ¿cómo se deben rotular los dos ejes?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.work: Number of tickets and price of one ticket
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió
workedExample.workEs: Número de boletos y precio de un boleto

onLevel.correctWork: The correct answer is Number of tickets and total cost. Each axis is labeled with one quantity from the problem — one axis shows the number of tickets and the other shows the total cost.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es Número de boletos y costo total. Cada eje se rotula con una cantidad del problema — un eje muestra el número de boletos y el otro muestra el costo total.
hints: Which TWO quantities change in this situation?
hintsEs: ¿Cuáles DOS cantidades cambian en esta situación?

practice.commonMistake: Reversing the coordinates of a point — writing (cost, tickets) instead of (tickets, cost). The independent variable always comes first in the ordered pair.

questions.stem: Songs cost $2 each. Which is the independent variable?
questions.explanation: The number of songs is what you choose. The total cost depends on that choice, so cost is the dependent variable.
questions.stemEs: Las canciones cuestan $2 cada una. ¿Cuál es la variable independiente?
questions.explanationEs: El número de canciones es lo que tú escoges. El costo total depende de esa elección, así que el costo es la variable dependiente.
choiceFeedback: This changes as a result of the choice made — it responds rather than causes.
This is a fixed rate, not something that changes as a result of a choice.
This isn't a quantity that changes at all in this relationship.
choiceFeedbackEs: Esto cambia como resultado de la elección hecha — responde en vez de causar.
Esta es una tarifa fija, no algo que cambie como resultado de una elección.
Esto no es una cantidad que cambie en esta relación.

questions.stem: "The longer you run, the more calories you burn." Which is the dependent variable?
questions.explanation: Calories burned depends on how long you run, so calories is the dependent variable.
questions.stemEs: «Mientras más tiempo corres, más calorías quemas.» ¿Cuál es la variable dependiente?
questions.explanationEs: Las calorías quemadas dependen de cuánto tiempo corres, así que las calorías son la variable dependiente.
choiceFeedback: This is what you choose or control — it's the one the other quantity responds to.
The runner is a person, not a changing quantity in this relationship.
Distance isn't mentioned as a changing quantity in this relationship.
choiceFeedbackEs: Esto es lo que tú eliges o controlas — es lo que hace que la otra cantidad responda.
El corredor es una persona, no una cantidad que cambia en esta relación.
La distancia no se menciona como una cantidad que cambie en esta relación.

questions.stem: A plant grows taller each day. Which sentence is correct?
choices: The number of days depends on height
Height depends on the number of days
Neither one depends on the other
questions.explanation: Days pass on their own; the height responds to them. So height is dependent and days is independent.
questions.stemEs: Una planta crece más alta cada día. ¿Qué oración es correcta?
choicesEs: El número de días depende de la altura
La altura depende del número de días
questions.explanationEs: Los días pasan solos; la altura responde a ellos. Así que la altura es dependiente y los días son independientes.
choiceFeedback: This has the two variables backward — days pass on their own, height responds.
One of these two quantities does respond to the other — they aren't unrelated.
Both quantities can't be independent — one has to respond to the other.
choiceFeedbackEs: Esto tiene las dos variables al revés — los días pasan por sí solos, la altura responde.
Una de estas dos cantidades sí responde a la otra — no son cosas sin relación.
Las dos cantidades no pueden ser independientes — una tiene que responder a la otra.

questions.stem: In any relationship between two quantities, the independent variable is the one that…
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the input you get to choose. The dependent variable responds to it.
questions.stemEs: En cualquier relación entre dos cantidades, la variable independiente es la que…
questions.explanationEs: La variable independiente es la entrada que tú puedes escoger. La variable dependiente responde a ella.
choiceFeedback: Size doesn't decide which variable is independent — being chosen does.
This describes what the DEPENDENT variable does, not the independent one.
Graph position doesn't decide which variable is independent — being chosen does.
choiceFeedbackEs: El tamaño no decide cuál variable es independiente — elegirla sí lo decide.
Esto describe lo que hace la variable DEPENDIENTE, no la independiente.
La posición en la gráfica no decide cuál variable es independiente — elegirla sí lo decide.

parallelPractice.stem: A table shows the relationship: x = 1 → y = 2, x = 2 → y = 4, x = 3 → y = 6. How does y change as x grows, and what is y when x = 5?

steps.prompt: Each time x goes up by 1, y goes up by ___.
steps.promptEs: Cada vez que x sube 1, y sube ___.
Así que y siempre es x × ___.
Cuando x = 5, y = 5 × 2 = ___.

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Read DOWN the y-column: the jump between rows is the rate the relationship runs on.

hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
